Kia India Announces Second Plant In Anantapur - USD 2 Billion Investment (Rs 18,800 Cr)

KS
By Kabir Sharma Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist • via Rushlane.com Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Rushlane.com Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Kia India has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Andhra Pradesh government to establish its second manufacturing plant in Anantapur.
  • The project involves a combined investment of USD 2 billion by Kia and its supplier partners, with production planned to begin in early 2030.
  • Official reporting verified via Rushlane.com news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • KABIR SHARMA Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist

Bharat NCAP Safety Standards & Indian Road Readiness

In India's rapidly evolving automotive landscape, crashworthiness and real-world durability are driving consumer purchase decisions like never before. As reported by Rushlane.com, indigenous automakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra are setting global safety benchmarks while optimizing suspension and ground clearance for unpredictable road conditions.

Big Picture: Upcoming monthly FADA retail delivery reports and Bharat NCAP rating scorecards will reveal which domestic models capture mass-market dominance.

Kia India has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Andhra Pradesh government to establish its second manufacturing plant in Anantapur. The project involves a combined investment of USD 2 billion by Kia and its supplier partners, with production planned to begin in early 2030. The new plant will have an installed capacity of 2 lakh vehicles a year, taking Kia’s total annual manufacturing capacity in India to 6.30 lakh units .

📌 The Core Development

The proposed facility and its supplier operations will cover a combined 465 acres. Kia expects the project to generate around 12,000 direct and indirect jobs . The new plant will carry out stamping, welding, painting and assembly, the same four manufacturing processes handled at Kia’s existing Anantapur facility.

Kia lists its current plant’s annual capacity at 4.30 lakh units. The additional 2 lakh units represent an increase of around 47%. The existing site covers 945 acres, including supplier operations, and supports 24,237 direct and indirect jobs, according to Kia. The company puts the initial investment by Kia and its suppliers at the first site at USD 2.9 billion, with cumulative investment across the two plants expected to reach up to USD 5 billion (Rs 47,000 crores).

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Kia says the second facility will manufacture new models across internal combustion and electric powertrains. The company has yet to name the models it will build there. Its existing plant produces the Seltos, Sonet, Syros, Carens, Carens Clavis, Carnival and Sorento. Kia’s current production mix in Anantapur already includes the Syros EV and Carens Clavis EV, CNG versions of the Carens and Carens Clavis, and the Sorento Hybrid.

Gwanggu Lee, Managing Director and CEO of Kia India , said the second plant would give the company more flexibility to respond to demand and introduce new models. He added that the expanded manufacturing base would serve both Indian and overseas markets.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Kia’s previously announced India roadmap targets annual sales of around 4.10 lakh units and a 7.6% market share by 2030. It also calls for eight electrified models, including hybrids and battery EVs, by the end of the decade. The Seltos Hybrid is expected in 2027, with hybrid versions of the Sonet and Carens planned by 2029. Kia has also outlined plans for another locally produced small electric SUV by 2029.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Those product timelines precede the second plant’s planned start of production in early 2030. Kia’s latest announcement leaves the allocation of those models across the two facilities open.

The Anantapur expansion follows Hyundai Motor Group’s October announcement of a USD 15.5 billion India investment programme for 2026–2032. That broader programme covers manufacturing, research and development, and supplier localisation. Kia’s latest MoU puts a location, production timeline and capacity figure on its own next phase of manufacturing expansion in India.
